To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
T. musculi is a self-limiting parasite of CBA mice and that the immune response to this parasite is characterized by the production of a wide range of antibody isotopes.
The immune response of CBA/H mice to T. musculi infection was characterized by a rapid and sustained antibody response to the parasite, with the production of IgM, IgG2a and IgG1.

The immunological response of the CBA mouse to infection with the mouse trypanosome, Trypanosoma mnsculi, is characterized by a rapid and strong antibody response, which is accompanied by the development of immunity to reinfection, and by a transient but marked depression of the immune response to sheep red cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular and cellular basis for host defence against trypanosome infection.
the immunological response of mice to the intracellular parasite Trypanosoma (Leptomonas) musculi.
the development and evaluation of novel approaches to the control of trypanosomiasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunological response of mice to T. musculi infection is complex and is dependent on the presence of both humoral and cell-mediated immune responses.
the immunological response to T. musculi is similar in many ways to that of the mouse to T. cruzi, and that the response is not a classical TH1/TH2 response.

the infection of CBA mice by T. musculi is controlled by a T-cell dependent response which is mediated by IgG2 antibodies and which is characterized by a rapid and transient phase of increasing parasitamia, followed by an equally rapid and stable phase of non-dividing parasites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T cells play an important role in the initial control of T. musculi infection, but that the subsequent development of immunity to the parasite is T-cell independent.
we have shown that the initial response to T. musculi in the mouse is a strong and complex immune response involving both antibody and T-cells.
the immune response to a primary infection of T. musculi in CBA mice is a complex and multi-faceted process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T cells play an essential role in the early control of T. musculi infection in mice.
the parasite is capable of producing a self-limiting, non-fatal infection, which induces a long-lasting, protective immunity in CBA mice.
the parasite is able to establish infection in the host, multiply and produce a self-limiting blood infection, but the infection is not cleared.
